text: When deploying Orbit to production, run the smoke-test suite first and only promote the build if it passes.
Before cutting an Orbit release, bump the version through the release workflow, never by hand-editing package files.
Any Acme Labs repository must enable branch protection on main before its first production deploy.
When a deploy fails its health check, roll back to the previous build before investigating.
When adding a new Orbit dependency, pin the exact version and wait out the release-age gate.
Every Acme Labs service must page the on-call engineer when its error budget is exhausted.
When deploying on a Friday after noon, get a second engineer's approval first.
We chose blue-green deploys for Orbit over rolling deploys, because instant rollback mattered more than the extra infrastructure cost.
Orbit will use SQLite on device instead of a hosted database, because offline operation is a core requirement.
Acme Labs picked a monorepo over per-app repositories, rejecting polyrepo because shared tooling drifted.
We decided deploys run from CI only, rejecting laptop deploys, because laptop builds were not reproducible.
Orbit adopted semantic-release for versioning rather than manual changelogs, to remove release-day mistakes.
Acme Labs standardised on pnpm over npm and yarn, because the workspace resolves reliably.
We chose to deploy during the Tuesday window rather than continuously, because support staffing is highest then.
The deploy broke production because we skipped the smoke tests; next time never promote a build without them.
Orbit's release failed when a version was edited by hand and the lockfile drifted; derive versions from the release tool instead.
Acme Labs lost a day when an expired audit allowlist turned CI red unexpectedly; track allowlist expiry dates ahead of time.
A rollback was slow because nobody had rehearsed it; rehearse the deploy rollback before each major release.
Orbit crashed on launch after a migration ran without a backup; always snapshot the database before migrating.
Acme Labs' outage lasted hours because alerts went to a retired channel; verify alert routing after every team change.
The Friday deploy caused a weekend incident; avoid shipping when nobody is around to respond.
Passing CI does not mean the deploy is safe: CI never exercises the production configuration, only the deploy smoke test does.
It looks like Orbit's version field can be edited directly, but semantic-release owns it and overwrites manual changes.
People assume Acme Labs' main branch is unprotected by default, but protection is already enforced by the organization ruleset.
A green health check does not mean the new build is serving traffic; the load balancer may still point at the old build.
Orbit's database looks like it syncs to the cloud, but it is local only and nothing is replicated.
Acme Labs staff often assume an alert resolving means the incident is over, but resolution only reflects the metric, not customer impact.
Deploys appear instant, but the cache takes up to ten minutes to clear, so users see the old version meanwhile.
